meta.title: Quiz 6 — Node.js & Server-Side Fundamentals
meta.description: Node.js runtime, npm, HTTP servers, sockets, modules, and server-side programming.

questions.questionMd: Which command correctly executes a JavaScript file called `app.js` using NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: `run node --file app.js`

options.label: B
options.text: `node app.js`

options.label: C
options.text: `execute app.js --runtime node`

options.label: D
options.text: `npm start app.js`

questions.explanationMd: A JavaScript file is executed with Node.js by writing `node` followed by the filename, such as `node app.js`.

questions.questionMd: In the context of networking, what is a socket?

options.label: A
options.text: A numbered logical endpoint, ranging from 0 to 65535, that identifies a specific service running on a host machine.

options.label: B
options.text: The encrypted tunnel created by HTTPS to protect data exchanged between a client browser and a remote web server.

options.label: C
options.text: One end of a communication channel through which data can be sent and received.

options.label: D
options.text: A physical hardware port on a server machine used to connect network cables to the motherboard.

questions.explanationMd: A socket represents one endpoint of a network communication channel. It is used by software to send and receive data over a network.

questions.questionMd: What is npm primarily used for in a NodeJS development workflow?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a version control system integrated with NodeJS that tracks changes to JavaScript source files across a development team.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a command-line tool that installs packages, libraries, and tools written in JavaScript and compatible with NodeJS.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a built-in NodeJS module that provides methods for creating HTTP servers and handling incoming TCP connections.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a browser extension that allows developers to inspect and modify the DOM of pages served from a NodeJS backend.

questions.explanationMd: npm is the Node package manager. It is mainly used to install and manage JavaScript packages and development tools.

questions.questionMd: What is the V8 engine, and what role does it play in both Chrome and NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a package manager integrated into NodeJS that downloads and manages third-party JavaScript libraries from the npm registry.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a DOM rendering engine that converts HTML and CSS into a visual pixel display inside the Chrome browser window.

options.label: C
options.text: It is the JavaScript interpreter used by both Chrome and NodeJS to parse, compile, and execute JavaScript code.

options.label: D
options.text: It is the network library embedded in Chrome that manages TCP connections and forwards HTTP messages to the operating system.

questions.explanationMd: V8 is Google's JavaScript engine. Chrome uses it to run JavaScript in the browser, and Node.js uses it to run JavaScript outside the browser.

questions.questionMd: Which curl command would you use to send an HTTP PUT request to `http://localhost:3000/hello`?

options.label: A
options.text: `curl --request PUT http://localhost:3000/hello`

options.label: B
options.text: `curl http://localhost:3000/hello --type PUT`

options.label: C
options.text: `curl --method PUT --Url http://localhost:3000/hello`

options.label: D
options.text: `curl PUT http://localhost:3000/hello`

questions.explanationMd: In curl, `--request PUT` explicitly sets the HTTP method to PUT for the specified URL.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the recommended way to send data in a POST request rather than using query parameters in the URL?

options.label: A
options.text: Append data to the URL path as route segments instead of query parameters so Express can read them from `req.params`.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the data in the body of the HTTP request rather than appending it as query parameters to the URL.

options.label: C
options.text: Store data in the browser's local storage before making the POST request so the server can retrieve it on the next GET request.

options.label: D
options.text: Encode all data as Base64 and place it in the Authorization header so the server can decode it securely upon receipt.

questions.explanationMd: POST requests commonly send data in the request body, which avoids putting the submitted data directly in the URL query string.

questions.questionMd: The NodeJS `on()` function used on a server object is the equivalent of which browser API?

options.label: A
options.text: `document.querySelector()`, which selects DOM elements matching a given CSS selector string.

options.label: B
options.text: `setTimeout()`, which schedules a callback function to be executed after a specified delay in milliseconds.

options.label: C
options.text: `addEventListener`, which registers a callback function to handle a specific named event.

options.label: D
options.text: `fetch()`, which asynchronously sends HTTP requests from the browser to a specified URL endpoint.

questions.explanationMd: In Node.js, `.on(eventName, callback)` registers a listener for a named event, similar to `addEventListener` in browser JavaScript.

questions.questionMd: If a NodeJS server is listening on port 3000 of your local machine, which URL would you use in a browser to access it?

options.label: A
options.text: `node://localhost:3000`

options.label: C
options.text: `http://localhost:3000`

options.label: D
options.text: `http://server:3000/local`

questions.explanationMd: A local HTTP server running on port 3000 can be reached through `http://localhost:3000` in the browser.

questions.questionMd: In a basic NodeJS server, what does `http.createServer()` return?

options.label: A
options.text: An active TCP connection to the operating system that immediately begins forwarding packets to the default HTTP port 80.

options.label: B
options.text: A Promise object that resolves with the first HTTP request received after the server begins listening on the specified port.

options.label: C
options.text: An Express application instance that provides routing methods such as `app.get()` and `app.post()`.

options.label: D
options.text: A Server object that can listen for incoming HTTP requests and emit events when requests arrive.

questions.explanationMd: `http.createServer()` creates and returns a Node.js HTTP Server object. That server can then listen on a port and respond to incoming requests.

questions.questionMd: What happens when you run the `node` command in a terminal without specifying a filename?

options.label: A
options.text: It starts an interactive REPL loop where you can type and execute JavaScript expressions one at a time, similar to the Chrome console.

options.label: B
options.text: It automatically searches the current directory for a file named `index.js` and executes it as the default entry point.

options.label: C
options.text: It prints the installed NodeJS version number and a list of available built-in modules, then exits immediately.

options.label: D
options.text: It launches a local HTTP server on port 80 and waits for incoming browser connections without executing any JavaScript.

questions.explanationMd: Running `node` alone opens the Node.js REPL, an interactive prompt where JavaScript expressions can be entered and evaluated.

questions.questionMd: What is "binding" in the context of running a server process?

options.label: A
options.text: Telling the operating system which port number to associate with the server process so it can receive incoming messages.

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing a persistent TCP connection between two servers so they can exchange data without repeating the handshake.

options.label: C
options.text: Encrypting the server's IP address so that DNS queries return a hashed value instead of the actual numerical address.

options.label: D
options.text: Compiling JavaScript source code into native machine code before the NodeJS runtime begins accepting HTTP requests.

questions.explanationMd: Binding a server to a port associates that server process with the port, allowing the operating system to route incoming connections to it.

questions.questionMd: What is the purpose of the `require()` statement in NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: It instructs the V8 engine to pre-compile a JavaScript file into bytecode and cache it for faster future execution.

options.label: B
options.text: It loads a module into the current file, similar to `import` in Java or `include` in C++.

options.label: C
options.text: It sends an HTTP GET request to the npm registry to check whether a package is compatible with the current NodeJS version.

options.label: D
options.text: It declares a global variable that is shared across all JavaScript files in the same NodeJS project directory.

questions.explanationMd: `require()` imports a module into the current Node.js file so its exported functionality can be used.

questions.questionMd: Which statement best describes server-side programming as opposed to client-side programming?

options.label: A
options.text: The code is compiled by the browser's JavaScript engine before being transmitted over TCP to the server for execution.

options.label: B
options.text: The code runs on a remote server that generates web pages and other web resources.

options.label: C
options.text: The code executes within a sandboxed environment provided by the operating system on the user's local machine.

options.label: D
options.text: The code runs inside the user's browser and is responsible for rendering HTML elements and handling DOM events directly.

questions.explanationMd: Server-side programming runs on a server and can generate pages, API responses, and other resources before sending them to clients.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) define?

options.label: A
options.text: The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server.

options.label: B
options.text: The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet.

options.label: C
options.text: The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols.

options.label: D
options.text: The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers.

questions.explanationMd: In this lecture context, TCP is presented as the lower-level protocol used to carry data for higher-level protocols such as HTTP and FTP over the network.

questions.questionMd: How does NodeJS handle the complexity of network sockets when building a web server?

options.label: A
options.text: NodeJS delegates all socket creation to the browser's DOM API, which then forwards messages to the server program.

options.label: B
options.text: NodeJS uses the V8 engine's built-in socket library to open encrypted connections on all available network ports.

options.label: C
options.text: NodeJS requires developers to manually create and bind sockets before attaching any HTTP request listeners.

options.label: D
options.text: NodeJS abstracts socket management away so developers do not need to think about sockets directly.

questions.explanationMd: Node.js HTTP server APIs hide most low-level socket-management details, letting developers work with server and request/response abstractions instead.
